title: PodcastsView
description: Create AggregatorApp/Podcasts/PodcastsView.swift mirroring the ThreadsView/TodayView pattern. Declare private enum LoadPhase { case loading, loaded, error(Error) }. Use @Environment(CredentialsStore.self), @State episodes array, nextCursor, phase, isFetchingNextPage, and LoadOnceGate. body: NavigationStack > Group switching on phase — .loading shows ProgressView; .error shows message + Retry button; .loaded shows not-configured ContentUnavailableView when !credentialsStore.isConfigured, empty ContentUnavailableView("No episodes", systemImage: "headphones") when empty, else GlassEffectContainer > List > ForEach with NavigationLink to PodcastPlayerView passing credentialsStore explicitly. Last-row .onAppear triggers loadNextPage. .refreshable calls loadFirstPage(showSpinner: false). .task loads first page via loadGate.
acceptance_criteria: Loading, loaded, error, not-configured, and empty states all render correctly
NavigationLink pushes PodcastPlayerView with credentialsStore passed explicitly
Scrolling to the last row triggers loadNextPage exactly once (isFetchingNextPage guard)
Pull-to-refresh calls loadFirstPage without spinner flash
loadNextPage silently fails on network error without changing phase

handoff_summary.completed: Implemented PodcastsView.swift with: private LoadPhase enum (loading/loaded/error); @Environment(CredentialsStore.self), @State episodes array, nextCursor, phase, isFetchingNextPage, LoadOnceGate; NavigationStack > Group switching on phase with ProgressView for loading, error VStack with Retry button for error, and inside loaded: not-configured ContentUnavailableView, empty ContentUnavailableView("No episodes", systemImage: "headphones"), or GlassEffectContainer > List > ForEach with NavigationLink to PodcastPlayerView(credentialsStore: credentialsStore); last-row .onAppear triggers loadNextPage; .refreshable on the GlassEffectContainer calls loadFirstPage(showSpinner: false); .task loads first page via loadGate (transitions to .loaded immediately when not configured); navigationTitle "Podcasts". Committed as [takt] B-dc4d0324.
handoff_summary.remaining: None for this bead. Downstream: tester bead will verify all states render correctly, pagination guard, and refresh behavior.
handoff_summary.risks: xcodebuild not available in worktree (CLI tools only, no Xcode); SourceKit diagnostics shown are index false-positives that clear once the project is indexed. Real compile verification deferred to tester/merge gate. PodcastsView must be wired into AppRoot.swift / the tab bar by a separate bead if not already done.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester verifies all acceptance criteria against the simulator: all states render, pagination guard, refresh without spinner flash, silent next-page failure, and navigationTitle.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: PodcastsView.swift is a new file with no overlap with existing files. The only conflict risk is if AppRoot.swift is also being modified by a sibling bead to wire in the Podcasts tab — file-scope separation means no actual conflict here.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: 1. not-configured check placed inside the .loaded phase (not before the switch as ThreadsView does) per spec description. The .task transitions immediately to .loaded when !credentialsStore.isConfigured, so the spinner is never stuck. 2. .refreshable placed on the GlassEffectContainer (not the NavigationStack) following the TodayView/ThreadsView pattern — pull-to-refresh must attach to scrollable content. 3. NavigationLink uses closure-form destination (not value-based) because PodcastPlayerView requires explicit credentialsStore injection via its init — value-based .navigationDestination cannot pass non-Hashable imperative parameters. 4. loadNextPage uses episode.id == episodes.last?.id (identity comparison) rather than index enumeration, avoiding stale index captures across async boundaries.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tester should verify: (1) Loading state shows ProgressView on first appear when configured; (2) Not-configured state shows ContentUnavailableView with gearshape icon without spinner when credentials absent; (3) Empty state shows headphones ContentUnavailableView after successful empty fetch; (4) Error state shows localizedDescription + Retry button, and Retry re-enters loadFirstPage; (5) Scrolling to last row calls loadNextPage exactly once per page (isFetchingNextPage guard prevents double-fetch); (6) Pull-to-refresh replaces episodes without spinner flash (showSpinner: false path); (7) Network error during loadNextPage leaves phase as .loaded and does not show error state; (8) navigationTitle is exactly "Podcasts".
handoff_summary.known_limitations: PodcastsView is created but not yet wired into the app's tab bar (AppRoot.swift). That is a separate bead responsibility. The compile step could not be verified with xcodebuild because only Xcode CLI tools are present in the worktree environment — merge gate tests will provide the authoritative build check.

conflict_risks: PodcastsView.swift is a new file with no overlap with existing files. The only conflict risk is if AppRoot.swift is also being modified by a sibling bead to wire in the Podcasts tab — file-scope separation means no actual conflict here.

# Developer Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

## Corrective bead scope

If your `bead_id` ends in `-corrective` or `-corrective-<N>` (e.g. `B-abc12345-corrective`, `B-abc12345-test-corrective-2`), you are running as a CORRECTIVE bead. Your scope is **strictly limited to fixing the specific failure that blocked the parent bead**. Do not:

- Add unrelated improvements, refactors, or cleanup, even if you notice them
- Reapply previously-reverted changes (the operator reverted them for a reason)
- Expand the surface area beyond what is needed to unblock the parent
- Touch files outside what the parent bead's `expected_files` / `expected_globs` covered, unless the failure is genuinely in another file and there is no smaller fix

If you notice an unrelated issue while fixing the corrective scope: **file a separate bead** via `takt bead create` describing what you saw, but do not fix it in this corrective. The operator will prioritize and dispatch.

When in doubt about scope: prefer the smallest possible fix. The reviewer of this corrective will check that the scope was respected.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Swift` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: ``.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

## Memory

**Read memory at bead start.** Before touching any code, run three searches using `$TAKT_CMD` (injected by the orchestrator):

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace global
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace specs
```

Treat results as ambient context — apply relevant entries; skip entries that don't apply.

**Write to memory when you discover reusable project knowledge** — something that would have changed your approach if you had known it upfront, and is not already in CLAUDE.md or the guardrails.

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<concise fact>" --namespace global               # project-wide knowledge
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<discovery>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>  # feature-scoped
```

Required Handoff Fields:

Every developer bead **must** populate the following three fields in its output JSON. Reviewers and tester agents rely on these fields to scope their work without additional back-and-forth turns. Use `"N/A"` only when a field is genuinely inapplicable (e.g., a trivial rename with no design trade-offs); do not leave fields blank.

- **`design_decisions`** — Document non-obvious architectural or implementation choices made during this bead. Include alternatives considered and why the chosen approach was preferred. Reviewers use this to evaluate correctness without re-deriving intent. Set to `"N/A"` only if the change was purely mechanical with no meaningful trade-offs.

- **`test_coverage_notes`** — Describe what the tester agent should verify: new code paths, edge cases introduced, regression risks, and any known untested scenarios left to the tester. Set to `"N/A"` only if the bead touched no executable code paths (e.g., documentation-only changes).

- **`known_limitations`** — Call out constraints, deferred work, or known gaps in the implementation. This includes out-of-scope items deliberately left for follow-up beads and any areas where the implementation is intentionally incomplete. Set to `"N/A"` if the implementation is complete as specified with no known gaps.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
- Populated `design_decisions`, `test_coverage_notes`, and `known_limitations` fields in every response.
